hero.title: Comprehensive Financial Planning
hero.subtitle: One Financial Plan Built Around Your Entire Life

blocks.text: Your investments, retirement income, taxes, estate plan, workplace benefits, and major life decisions all affect one another. Managing each separately can create gaps, missed opportunities, and conflicting strategies.

PointOak brings those pieces together through comprehensive financial planning built around your goals. Instead of focusing on one account or one decision at a time, we create an integrated plan that helps you see the full picture and make informed financial decisions with confidence.
As your financial life becomes more complex, individual decisions become harder to separate.

A retirement withdrawal can affect your taxes. A Roth conversion may influence Medicare costs. An estate planning decision can change how assets should be titled or invested. A job change can create new questions about retirement accounts, equity compensation, and cash flow.
Comprehensive financial planning looks at those decisions together.
Rather than managing investments, retirement, taxes, and estate considerations in isolation, PointOak creates one coordinated strategy designed around where you are today and where you want to go.

items.title: Bring Every Part of Your Financial Life Together

body.text: We organize your investments, retirement accounts, income sources, estate considerations, workplace benefits, and other financial priorities into one coordinated plan.
That gives you a clearer view of what you have, what needs attention, and how individual decisions affect the bigger picture.

items.title: Plan for Retirement With Greater Clarity

body.text: We help you understand whether you're on track for retirement and how different decisions may affect your future.
That can include projected income needs, Social Security, pensions, retirement account withdrawals, investment strategy, and other factors that influence when and how you can retire.
Taxes can affect nearly every part of a financial plan.

We incorporate tax-aware considerations into investment management, retirement withdrawals, Roth conversions, charitable strategies, and other planning decisions while working with your CPA or tax professional as appropriate.
segs: , retirement withdrawals, Roth conversions, charitable strategies, and other planning decisions while working with your CPA or tax professional as appropriate.

body.text: Estate documents are only one piece of legacy planning.

We help coordinate beneficiary designations, investment accounts, retirement assets, and your broader financial plan with the work of your estate attorney so your intentions remain aligned as circumstances change.

items.title: Give You One Central Point of Contact

body.text: You may already have a CPA, attorney, insurance professional, or other advisors.
PointOak helps connect the pieces. We serve as a central financial resource, coordinating with your other professionals so you aren't left managing separate recommendations on your own.
A financial plan shouldn't sit untouched for years.
We regularly review your strategy and make adjustments as your goals, family, career, investments, tax laws, and other circumstances evolve.

sections.title: Is Comprehensive Financial Planning Right for You?

blocks.lead: This service may be a good fit if you:
items: Are approaching or preparing for retirement.
Have investments spread across multiple accounts.
Work with several financial, tax, or legal professionals who aren't coordinating.
Recently received an inheritance or other significant assets.
Sold a business or experienced another liquidity event.
Receive executive compensation, RSUs, or stock options.
Are considering a 401(k) rollover or Roth conversion.
Want your investment strategy connected to your broader life goals.
Feel like your financial life has become too complex to manage piece by piece.

body.text: We begin by learning about your goals, family, assets, income, concerns, and what prompted you to seek advice.
We review your complete financial picture so we understand not only where you are today, but what you're working toward.

We create an integrated financial strategy that connects investment management, retirement planning, tax-aware decisions, estate coordination, workplace benefits, and other priorities relevant to your situation.
Every recommendation is designed within the context of the full plan rather than as an isolated decision.
We help put the plan into action, coordinate with your other professionals when needed, and continue monitoring your progress.
As life changes, your financial plan changes with it.

blocks.text: Comprehensive planning only works when your advisor understands the whole picture.
At PointOak, you'll work directly with an experienced advisor who knows your financial goals, understands the different parts of your plan, and stays involved over time.
Our background in both private wealth management and corporate retirement plans gives us a broad perspective on the decisions that affect individuals and families throughout their financial lives.

blocks.text: As an independent, fee-only fiduciary firm, we don't earn commissions from products or receive compensation for recommending one investment over another. Our role is to provide thoughtful guidance designed around your goals.

It can include investment management, retirement income planning, tax-aware strategies, estate coordination, workplace benefits, insurance considerations, major life events, and other financial decisions that affect your long-term goals.

items.q: How is comprehensive financial planning different from investment management?

a.text: Investment management focuses primarily on your portfolio.
Comprehensive financial planning looks beyond the portfolio to consider how investments interact with retirement, taxes, estate planning, income, workplace benefits, and other financial priorities.
At PointOak, investment management is integrated into the broader financial plan rather than treated as a standalone decision.

items.q: What should a comprehensive financial plan include?

a.lead: The exact plan depends on your situation, but it may include:
items: Cash flow and major financial decisions.
The goal is to connect the areas that affect one another rather than manage each separately.

items.q: When should I start comprehensive financial planning?

a.text: You don't need to wait until retirement.

Comprehensive planning can become especially valuable when your financial life grows more complex—such as approaching retirement, changing careers, receiving an inheritance, selling a business, managing executive compensation, or coordinating multiple investment and retirement accounts.
Starting earlier can also provide more time to evaluate decisions that may benefit from multi-year planning.

items.q: Do you work with my CPA and estate attorney?

a.text: Yes.

PointOak does not provide tax or legal advice, but we can coordinate with your existing CPA, attorney, and other professionals so financial decisions are considered within the context of your broader plan.
That helps reduce the risk of different professionals making recommendations without visibility into the rest of your financial picture.

items.q: How often will my financial plan be reviewed?

a.text: We review financial plans regularly and revisit them when circumstances warrant. Major life changes, retirement decisions, market conditions, tax-law changes, significant purchases, changes in income, or other events may create a reason to update the analysis between scheduled reviews.

items.q: Do I need a financial plan if I'm already working with an investment advisor?

a.text: Possibly.

If your current advisor is primarily managing your investments, you may still benefit from broader planning that coordinates retirement income, taxes, estate considerations, workplace benefits, and other financial decisions.
One useful question to ask is whether your advisor is managing your portfolio or actively coordinating your complete financial picture.

items.q: Is comprehensive financial planning only for retirees?

a.text: No.
PointOak works with individuals and families across several stages of life, including accumulation, pre-retirement, active retirement, and wealth transition.
The planning priorities change over time, but the value of coordinating financial decisions can begin well before retirement.

items.q: How much does comprehensive financial planning cost?

a.text: PointOak offers comprehensive financial planning as part of certain ongoing wealth-management relationships and may also provide financial planning through a separate planning engagement. Fees depend on the scope and complexity of the services provided and are discussed before an engagement begins. The initial consultation is complimentary.

sections.title: Planning for the Decisions You Haven't Made Yet

blocks.text: A comprehensive financial plan isn't valuable simply because it produces projections.
It's valuable when it helps you evaluate real decisions.

items: Should I retire this year or work another two years?
Should I pay off my mortgage or keep more assets invested?
Should I make a Roth conversion this year?
Can I afford to buy a second home?
How should I invest an inheritance or other significant cash event?
Should I exercise or hold company stock?
How much can I give to my children without compromising my own retirement?
Should I claim Social Security now or wait?
How would a major market decline affect my retirement plan?
The answer isn't always obvious from looking at one account.
PointOak helps evaluate these decisions in the context of your complete financial picture.

sections.title: See the Impact Before Making the Decision

blocks.text: Financial planning becomes more useful when you can compare alternatives rather than simply receive a static projection.
PointOak uses interactive financial-planning technology to help model different scenarios and evaluate how changes could affect your broader financial plan.
Depending on your circumstances, we can evaluate questions such as:

items: Claim Social Security now vs. later

blocks.text: This allows us to discuss the tradeoffs between different decisions before putting a strategy into action.

body.text: Clients also have access to a secure planning portal where they can view their financial information, connect accounts, review planning results, and securely exchange documents with PointOak.
